Yes, everyone should use long ass passwords that are unique for each account. Yes, everyone should use a password keeper to manage all these unique, long ass passwords. But almost everyone does neither. They will use the simplest password a site permits, and they will reuse that password as often as possible across the internet. Something a user has (smart phone) is way more secure than something they know (the likely weak password most users will choose).

If you look at password databases people collect from breaches, you'll see most humans tend to choose the same passwords other humans use. Guessing against such a list is much less time consuming than trying to crack a password by brute force. And far, far easier than stealing all your intended victims' phones.
